Answer: F
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a prominent right paratracheal opacity with lobulated contours, which is the classic radiographic appearance of right paratracheal lymphadenopathy. While other masses like bronchogenic cysts can occur in this location, they typically present as smooth, well-defined round lesions, whereas the irregular widening seen here strongly suggests enlarged lymph nodes.
